reply:
Still word splitting. Quoting `"$f"` is too late—the split happens in `$(ls *.csv)` before the loop assigns to `f`. The unquoted `$(ls)` output is split into words first; the loop receives those already-split words. Quoting `"$f"` protects it only after assignment.

If you have a file `q3 report.csv`, the `$(ls)` produces that exact string, then the unquoted expansion splits it into `q3` and `report.csv` as two separate loop iterations. `process "q3"` runs (file doesn't exist), then `process "report.csv"` runs (half a filename).

What would change my mind: the exact output of `$(ls *.csv)` and which specific files are being skipped, so I can see if something else is filtering them.

grade.note: Reply correctly explains that word splitting occurs during $(ls) expansion before assignment, matching the ground truth, though it also asks for extra confirmation.
